newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sporadic strikes dog Air France Europe.
newsitem.headline: Sporadic strikes dog Air France Europe.

text.p: Ground staff and some pilots at Air France Europe staged sporadic strikes on Wednesday in a continuing dispute over wage and working conditions, but the state-owned airline said the protests failed to disrupt flights.

An airline spokeswoman said flights were operating normally although several ground staff unions asked staff at Paris' Orly airport to stop work for more than three-and-a-half hours in every eight-hour shift.
One union representing about one third of the airline's pilots called on members to stop work from 1 p.m. (1100 GMT to midnight (2200 GMT).
Talks on the dispute broke down on Tuesday night. Unions, complaining their minimum demands were not being met, accused management of seeking to spread negotiations over six months.
The protesters deliberately ignored threats by management to impose sanctions on strikers if they failed to abide by a legal requirement to give five-day notice for the stoppages.
The airline, citing unexplained "technical reasons", sacked the head of its European operations, Michel Ennesser. Unions saw the decision as a sanction for failing to prevent the dispute.

Air France Europe's operations at Orly airport, south of Paris, have been dogged since last week by strikes to protest against the unifying of more generous pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France.
Air France began this week leasing the activities and staff of Air France Europe, the former Air Inter domestic airline, in a key step this week towards a full merger set for September.
Management says terms need to be brought more into line with those of lower-cost competitors such as British Airways as deregulation takes effect on European Union domestic routes.
